title: N1 City Mall held fully liable after Cape Town woman slips on melted ice cream
text: N1 City Mall held fully liable after Cape Town woman slips on melted ice cream The Western Cape High Court has found N1 City Mall’s owners, managing agent and cleaning contractor jointly liable for damages suffered by a shopper who slipped on a substance resembling melted ice cream in 2014. Image: Ai-Generated The Western Cape High Court in Cape Town has held the parties responsible for the management and cleaning of N1 City Mall liable for thein a passageway at the shopping centre. The respondents in the matter were Fountainhead Property Trust and Sycom Property Trust, the mall’s owners, and Bidvest Cleaning Ltd, the cleaning contractor. Broll Property Group Ltd, the mall’s managing agent, was also involved in the appeal.and Dennis Davis handed down the judgment on October 28, 2026, overturning an earlier ruling that found the woman, E Louw, 20% responsible for her own injuries.The incident happened at N1 City Mall in Goodwood on Workers’ Day, May 1, 2014, during the lunchtime period. The appeal court ruled that the first to fourth defendants were jointly and severally liable for 100% of the damages Louw could prove she had suffered. The ruling followed an appeal against the trial court’s decision, which had found the mall’s owners and managing agent, Broll Property Group, liable but absolved Bidvest Cleaning of responsibility.Louw’s claim arose from a slip-and-fall incident in a passageway at the shopping centre, where she slipped on a substance that appeared to be melted ice cream. The trial court had found the mall owners and Broll liable but reduced their liability by 20%, concluding that Louw had contributed to the accident through her own negligence.However, the appeal court reconsidered both the adequacy of the cleaning arrangements and whether Louw should have been held partly responsible for the incident. The court found that the cleaning system in place was inadequate for a busy public holiday, when the shopping centre could reasonably expect substantial pedestrian traffic and an increased risk of spills.Evidence showed that cleaners’ rounds could take about 40 minutes, while the system largely depended on cleaners discovering spills during their rounds or being alerted by members of the public or security personnel. The court also raised concerns about the staffing arrangements and the evidence available to establish whether cleaners were present and properly supervised. It found that the defendants had failed to demonstrate that reasonable measures had been taken to keep the passageways safe for shoppers.The appeal court found that Bidvest, as the cleaning contractor, had a legal duty to take reasonable steps to protect members of the public from foreseeable hazards. The court said the contractor should have anticipated the need for additional cleaning staff on a public holiday and could not simply rely on the mall owners or Broll to request more personnel.Court rejects finding that woman was negligent The appeal court also rejected the finding that Louw should bear 20% of the responsibility for her injuries. It found that shoppers were entitled to expect that walkways in a shopping centre would be reasonably safe and were not required to constantly look down at the floor while walking.The court accordingly amended the original order to hold the first to fourth defendants jointly and severally liable for 100% of the damages Louw could prove. The judgment establishes liability for the incident, but the amount of damages payable to Louw is yet to be decided.
summary: N1 City Mall held fully liable after Cape Town woman slips on melted ice cream The Western Cape High Court has found N1 City Mall’s owners, managing agent and cleaning contractor jointly liable for damages suffered by a shopper who slipped on a substance resembling melted ice cream in 2014. The appeal court ruled that the first to fourth defendants were jointly and severally liable for 100% of the damages Louw could prove she had suffered.
